covers.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: a polished technical-article cover, wide landscape 16:9, ideally 2048 x 1152.
Create a NEW cover for the article "Roofline: building a performance budget from compute and memory bandwidth". The previous abstract industrial sculpture was rejected because its connection to Roofline was not recognizable. This new cover must be immediately identifiable as the Roofline performance model, even as a thumbnail.
Design: premium Swiss editorial data visualization, bold typography, elegant scientific graphic, highly polished but clear. Warm ivory paper background, midnight navy graph region, vivid cobalt for memory-bound slope, bright mint for compute ceiling, subtle precision grid. Use tasteful luminous line depth and a few translucent material accents to make it fancy. It is a meaningful chart-led editorial cover, not a generic technology scene.
Composition:
Top 20 percent: large unmistakable title "ROOFLINE" at left. Under it, smaller text "Compute, bandwidth, and performance". Small "00" at upper right.
Center 65 percent: one large clear 2D schematic Roofline graph with TWO normal axes: vertical Performance, horizontal Arithmetic intensity. The graph must have exactly ONE continuous roofline upper boundary: start at the lower-left origin, slope linearly upward toward the middle, turn sharply at a single ridge, then remain perfectly horizontal across the entire right half. This is the performance upper bound P <= min(F, BW * I). Use cobalt for the rising segment and mint for the horizontal segment, with very subtle dimensional extrusion or light on the lines. The rising segment is the bandwidth bound, the flat segment is the peak compute ceiling. No extra lines above the ceiling. No peaks, waves, loops, staircases, or descending portions.
Place the text "MEMORY-BOUND" in the left region underneath the rising segment, and "COMPUTE-BOUND" in the right region underneath the flat segment. Clearly readable, no ambiguity. Put "BW × I" just above the rising line and "F" just above the flat line.
Mark the ridge with one visible small circle and a thin dotted guide straight down to the horizontal axis; label that horizontal-axis point "F / BW".
Horizontal axis label exactly "Arithmetic intensity (FLOP/Byte)"; vertical axis label exactly "Performance (FLOP/s)". No numeric ticks or invented measured values; this is a conceptual model.
Bottom band: one crisp formula "P ≤ min(F, BW × I)" with a short quiet line "Memory traffic → Compute throughput".
Typography: sharp, restrained, perfectly legible sans-serif and technical monospaced accents. No Chinese text. These exact brief labels are important.
Constraints: clearly preserve the scientifically correct rising-then-flat roofline shape and association of labels with the correct regions. Label the x-axis intensity, not time. No GPU product shot, no giant decorative chip, no random glass sculpture, no brain, no robot, no brand logos, no watermark, no invented benchmark data. Prioritize conceptual clarity and an excellent editorial composition over decorative details.

Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: technical article cover for an AI infrastructure engineering blog.
Input image: STYLE REFERENCE ONLY, the approved Roofline cover. Create a different diagram for the article described below; do not copy its graph, formula or topic.
Match the approved cover's design language closely: landscape 16:9, warm ivory header and footer, oversized bold black Swiss sans-serif headline, small chapter number in upper right, a generous midnight-navy central technical grid, precise electric-blue and mint-green diagrams with restrained glow. Refined, impressive, editorial, directly about the technical subject. Keep all labels legible and well separated. Front-facing crisp technical illustration, not abstract 3D sculpture. The central diagram occupies about 60% of image height. Header about 24%, footer about 14%. Retain generous safe margins; never clip text. No logos, watermarks, benchmark numbers, invented speedups or decorative unrelated objects. Use only the English text specified below and ordinary diagram arrows.
Headline "COMMUNICATION", chapter "01". Subtitle "Collectives, bandwidth, and topology".
Central diagram: a clean conceptual two-node topology. Left enclosure "NODE A" contains FOUR chips labeled GPU 0, GPU 1, GPU 2, GPU 3, linked as a simple rectangular ring with blue bidirectional links, caption "NVLink". Right enclosure "NODE B" similarly contains FOUR GPU chips labeled GPU 4, GPU 5, GPU 6, GPU 7 linked as a ring. At the inner edge of each node place a distinct "NIC" box connected to its local GPU fabric with a short line labeled "PCIe". Connect the two NIC boxes with a long mint bidirectional link labeled "RDMA". Node enclosures must be clearly separate; the inter-node link must connect NIC to NIC, never GPU directly. Diagram is schematic, not a specification of a particular SKU. Below the topology within the navy panel, show a simple three-part semantic strip "Reduce-scatter" + "All-gather" → "All-reduce". Do not draw imaginary all-to-all mesh over every GPU.
Footer formula exactly "T ≈ steps × α + bytes / BW". Secondary footer text "Latency · Traffic · Topology". Prioritize the interconnect topology and the equation as the visual meaning.

Central diagram: five evenly spaced tall columns separated by subtle vertical rules. Large white labels at top of columns: "TP", "DP", "EP", "CP", "PP".
TP column: a single square weight matrix divided into four differently tinted vertical shards, each shard linked downward to a separate small device. Caption "Tensor shards".
DP column: two identical small complete model blocks labeled "Model", each receiving its own distinct blue or green token row. Caption "Model replicas".
EP column: four separate rectangular expert blocks with sparse token routing arrows selecting different experts. Caption "Expert shards".

These are five DIFFERENT visual mechanisms, not five identical network diagrams. Keep each separate and balanced. Minimal notation, high readability.
Footer "Weights · KV state · Activations · Communication". Secondary small footer "Capacity and latency shape the choice". No performance values or claims of one strategy being always best.

Middle group labeled "PREFILL": stacked input token rows feed matrix tiles; nearby stacked memory blocks clearly labeled "KV cache". A prominent MINT arrow labeled "KV transfer" connects this middle group to the right group.
